newsitem.title: USA: Illinois agency targets Allstate for bond program.
newsitem.headline: Illinois agency targets Allstate for bond program.

text.p: Illinois Development Finance Authority and Allstate Corp's Allstate Insurance Co are working to develop a public/private relationship that would enable social service agencies to raise funds through bond issues for capital projects.

Bobby Wilkerson, the authority's director, said Wednesday that bond deals are in the works for two non-profit, 501(c)3 agencies that are largely dependent on funding through state of Illinois contracts and would have difficult time selling debt in the open market.
He said "substantial discussions" have been held with Allstate officials about the Northbrook, Ill.-based insurer purchasing the bonds with limited credit enhancement.

Instead of a letter of credit or bond insurance, Wilkerson said the authority would provide credit enhancement through $10 million of funds appropriated for that purpose by the Illinois General Assembly. That structure, he said, would lower the cost of the deal for the borrower.

Pending deals involve a group of African-American human services agencies on Chicago's southside that have about $15 million of capital needs, and a mental health clinic in Decatur with an approximately $4 million issue, according to Wilkerson.
Proceeds from the issues would fund the acquisition or rehabilitation of facilities, he added.
He added that the social service groups provide essential services to the state on a contract basis and receive 90 percent to 95 percent of their funding as a result of those contracts.
"We call this socially responsible investing," Wilkerson said. "We know people won't give money away, but the buyer feels good about it."
Allstate officials were not immediately available to comment on the program.

Wilkerson said the bond issues are structured like any other bond deals, with bankers and bond counsel. Senior bankers on the deals from First Chicago Capital Markets and First of America Securities Inc. were not available to comment.
Wilkerson said the authority's board generally approved the concept at its meeting Wednesday. Final approval of the deals was postponed until the board's December meeting.
Wilkerson said the authority would not have an exclusive relationship with Allstate in these types of deals and would welcome other institutional buyer involvement.
Allstate is a major owner of municipal bonds with $16 billion of munis in its portfolio at the end of 1995, according to a report the company released in August.
